A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WILDCAT research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–M are readable and can be reliably aligned.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Tables 2–4 report original BigGAN image-generation, T2T-ViT classification, and LongBench-E cache-compression experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds FlashAttention 2 comparisons, query/key growth measurements, compression settings, and parameter-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same randomly pivoted Nyström selection, optimal weighting, recentering, temperature selection, binning, and weighted-attention procedures. No algorithmic modification is documented.

E1.justification: The image-generation, image-classification, and 13 LongBench-E tasks remain. Section 4.4 adds an attention-approximation scenario using independent Gaussian queries, keys, and values. The new QASPER-E diagnostic uses data already represented in the retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.4 adds FlashAttention 2 as an explicitly evaluated, optimized exact-attention comparator. The five approximate-attention competitors and five cache-compression competitors in the existing application benchmarks remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from one cache-compression level to three and adds Gaussian timing/error experiments with d=64, r=64, B=16, and sequence lengths 2^13–2^18, plus rank/bin sweeps. A new diagnostic averages measurements over layers and ten eligible QASPER sequences. Original vision settings remain unchanged. Table 4 labels the intermediate compression level 87.5%, whereas Section 4.3 says 87.75%.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial analyses absent from v1: sensitivity to compression severity in Table 4, empirical examination of theoretical growth assumptions in Table 5, rank/bin time–accuracy trade-offs in Figure M.1, and a prefill-overhead comparison in Appendix M.3.

E5.justification: Appendix M.4 newly reports 100 replicates, median runtime, and mean approximation error for the FlashAttention 2 experiment. Existing vision results retain the same five-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting; their changed numerical deviations are result updates.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported vision settings, BigGAN speed-up changes from 3.71× to 4.33× and IS degradation from 1.40±0.55% to 1.22±0.87%. Classification accuracy changes from 82.18±0.03% to 82.19±0.04%, with layer speed-ups changing from 11.60×/2.77× to 11.59×/2.65×. Added results include compression averages of 42.12 and 36.55, FlashAttention 2 speed-ups of 1.1×–68×, growth-statistic and parameter-sweep results, and SnapKV/COMPRESSKV prefill times of 3.38/3.43 seconds.

T1.justification: Section 3 restores the missing 1/p! factor in the Taylor-matrix definition, consistent with the existing Appendix E expansion. Appendix D, Equation 11 corrects the denominator's eigenvalue index from i to l. V2 also adds a norm-conversion argument extending the stated error comparison to operator and row norms; the principal theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims: near-linear attention approximation with super-polynomial error decay, efficient implementation, and benefits for image generation, classification, and cache compression. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets measured Qwen/QASPER growth statistics as supporting applicability of Corollary 2. Appendix M.3 discusses accepting prefill costs when memory is the bottleneck. Existing limitations concerning causal masking, sequential pivoting, and other kernels remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix M.4 newly specifies PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130 for the added FlashAttention 2 experiments. Existing hardware disclosures, software settings for the original benchmarks, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dao's FlashAttention 2 work and Veličković et al. on bounded query/key norms, and expands comparison with prior norm guarantees. The Qwen2 reference is replaced by the Qwen2.5 technical report. Most other bibliography changes update metadata rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall organization are retained. V2 adds localized explanations and subsections 4.4 and M.4, updates publication and acknowledgment text, and cleans up bibliographic formatting.

P2.justification: Table 4 expands into three compression-level blocks. New Table 5, Figure 3, and Figure M.1 introduce growth measurements, a dual-axis scaling plot, and parameter trade-off displays, substantially expanding the empirical presentation. The existing methodology diagram and generated-image examples are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single compression budget and absence of a FlashAttention 2 comparison, v2 better tests compression tolerance, practical speed, and prefill cost, while correcting two mathematical expressions. The gains are limited by the synthetic FlashAttention 2 inputs and finite, averaged norm measurements, which alone cannot establish asymptotic assumptions. The 87.5%/87.75% reporting inconsistency introduces a small clarity defect.
